newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-FKI going to the line for Newman Tonks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-FKI going to the line for Newman Tonks.

text.p: British engineering group FKI Plc said on Monday that it had received acceptances regarding 20.45 percent shareholding in building equipment group Newman Tonks Plc.
Analysts said it might have to wait until the last minute to pull off a takeover, but said FKI was in a strong position to win.
FKI said it had received valid acceptances for 26,162,400 shares as on January 10, as part of its 195.7 million pound ($327.6 million) hostile bid for Newman Tonks launched last December.
FKI said it had extended its offer to 1500 GMT on January 24, 1996 as it urged Newman Tonks shareholders again to accept the offer.
FKI had said on December 16 that it had received undertakings from two main institutional shareholders -- M&G Group and Britannic Assurance -- in respect of some 13.37 percent of Newman shares.
It has been able to muster just over seven percent in the last three weeks, and analysts remained optimistic on Monday about FKI seeking the necessary acceptances for gaining control.
"FKI is in a strong position, I think the timing is perfect," said an analyst with a London brokerage who declined to be named.

FKI's cash-and-shares offer for Newman Tonks, currently equivalent to 153 pence a share, at the time of the offer represented a 46.3 percent premium to the firm's closing share price of 102.5 pence on December 13 just before Newman said it had received the offer on December 15.
Newman traded within the 150/155 pence range towards close of Monday trade in a low volume trade of about 12,000 shares.

Newman Tonks urges shareholders to reject the offer saying the bid failed to reflect its "profitable development in international markets,its restructuring... and its strengthening order book in major British product areas.

The company repeated its rejection of the bid on Monday saying its prospects were "now excellent". "... And the board reiterates that the offer (by FKI) is wholly inadequate," it said in its response.
Newman said its management had "successfully repositioned and refocused" the group.

"It is now an international business poised to benefit from its expansion into continental Europe and the USA as well as from the expected upturn in construction markets, particularly in the UK," it said.

The company said it would be writing to shareholders to provide further information about the group's businesses and prospects including a profit estimate and dividend forecast for the year ended December 31, 1996.
However, some analysts said that the fact that M&G has already accepted the offer could prove favourable for FKI.
M&G owns 11.8 percent in Newman Tonks.
"....The small shareholder has got the message that the valuation is reasonable," said an analyst.
"The choice will be...which management they would like to stick on with," he said.
The building sector in Britain and rest of Europe has been sluggish in the last three years, reflecting in the share price of Newman Tonks which traded as low as 98 pence in 1996.
Analysts claimed the shares traded more than 50 percent discount relative to the FT All share index since December 1991.
UK's commercial property sector -- a big market for Newman -- is seen looking up in the second half of 1997 with reflections in balance sheet expected in 1998.
FKI's chairman Jeff Whalley had said Newman Tonks represented an opportunity to expand FKI's hardware group internationally and in new sectors of the market.
FKI's share price held firm at 205 pence in a moderate turnover of 1.29 million shares.
